review_scope: Complete 73-line concept and seven-line default-availability reusable read, including front matter, headings, all31 parsed candidates, non-candidate context and editorial expiry comments. Multi-license rules retain usually/almost-always qualifications and per-policy exceptions. No effective billing/seat/policy observation, live provider terms, rendered assurance, adoption, rights or independent omission certification.

claims.statement: The enterprise/organization policy concept uses the Copilot feature scope; actual seat, product and rendered availability need separate evidence.
Enterprise AI controls and organization settings govern feature, agent and model access and use, including a CLI-access example.
Enterprise-level policies are set before organization-level policies; organization controls cannot be interpreted in isolation.
Most enterprise policies allow explicit enablement, disablement or delegation to organizations; this is not an unconditional least-privilege default.
Cloud-agent access is an exception allowing an enterprise to choose the exact organizations receiving access.
Enterprise-assigned users are not covered by Let organizations decide through an organization seat.
A separate Policies for enterprise-assigned users setting determines enabled/disabled defaults for delegated policies affecting directly assigned users.
Generally, policies govern users licensed by the corresponding Business/Enterprise organization or enterprise, not everyone who accesses its repositories.
Some explicitly described policies govern everyone in enterprise repositories, including blocking cloud agent; this is a scope exception to seat-based governance.
Across differently configured organizations in one enterprise, the least-restrictive policy usually applies, with policy-specific exceptions.
Across licenses from different enterprises, the most-restrictive policy almost always applies, with exceptions; any-enterprise disabling of GitHub Chat is the example.
For model policies on a Team plan, model access is determined by the organization paying for usage rather than a universal multi-license rule.
Usage billed to on the Copilot features page is the described route for identifying that paying organization; no billing state is observed.
The page states an individual plan is cancelled when the user joins Business/Enterprise, preventing the described personal/enterprise policy conflict; actual plan transition remains unverified.
The policy-conflicts reference is required for per-policy exceptions; usually/almost-always rules are insufficient for a universal evaluator.
Unconfigured GA feature/model defaults are supplied by a separately reviewed reusable; explicit settings and defaults are distinct.
The linked default-availability concept requires independent review, not certification through a link.
Policies can cover authenticated Copilot use in IDEs, GitHub website and CLI, but this statement is not complete per-policy surface coverage.
Not every policy applies on every surface; assess the supported-surfaces reference independently.
GitHub Copilot app and Copilot CLI have separate independent client policies, allowing one without the other.
Excess policy-setting access and unclear governance communication can cause drift; compliance risk is not proof that a target has drifted.
Regular review of policy administrators is recommended; enterprise and organization permissions must be examined separately.
Enterprise policy administrators include enterprise owners or holders of Manage enterprise AI controls custom-role permission.
Organization policy administrators include organization owners or relevant granular custom-permission holders.
Audit logs should monitor policy changes and organization enablement; audit collection is not enforcement or accepted change approval.
Enterprise and organization setting procedures are distinct linked documents; only the organization document is already fully reviewed in this workstream.
Business/Enterprise default-availability uses separate policies for unconfigured generally available features and unconfigured generally available models.
Each default-availability policy chooses enabled or disabled; enabled defaults can introduce latest features/models without per-item administrator intervention.
The reusable marks its temporary activation-status text with an editorial expiry of October 22, 2026; expiry is source-maintenance metadata, not executable authority.
The pin says the model default policy is already active but the feature default policy will become active soon; preserve staged activation and do not invent a concrete feature activation date.
